title: Trump and Beijing Dismiss the AI Slowdown as Microsoft Drafts 'Humanist AI' Rules
sources: The Neuron, The Rundown AI, Morning Brew, 1440 Daily Digest (Sep 15)
tldr: Trump and China's government both dismissed Anthropic's call to slow AI development as "fear-mongering" and a "hoax," and AI-linked stocks sold off on the uncertainty.
Microsoft AI drafted a "Humanist AI" code of conduct requiring its future models to always yield to human control — a template worth borrowing for your own client guardrails.
The 10-year Treasury yield topped 5% for the first time since 2023, raising borrowing costs behind any client business case built on cheap debt.

tips.heading: Let AI draft freely, then check constraints in a second pass
steps: Ask the AI to solve or draft its best answer first, with no rules applied yet.
Give it your non-negotiables afterward: word count, required facts, formatting, tests, safety rules.
Have it check and revise the final result against every constraint before returning it.
tips.prompt: Solve this for quality first. Then run a separate final pass against these non-negotiable constraints: [RULES]. Fix every violation before giving me the final answer.

tips.heading: Prove one agent can't do the job before building it an org chart
steps: Give one long-context agent the entire job end-to-end before splitting it into specialized sub-agents.
Only build an agent "org chart" if that single agent demonstrably fails.
If you split it, watch the handoffs — a summary can silently drop a detail the next agent needed.
Polylane made this swap and cut median time-to-PR from 2.2 hours to 35 minutes, cost from $111 to $18.

news.body: Trump and China's government both dismissed Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call to slow AI development. Trump called it a "hoax" on Truth Social and said a "high IQ" president is the only guardrail AI needs; China's Foreign Ministry and state media called the plan "fear-mongering." AI-linked stocks (Nvidia, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, SoftBank) sold off on the uncertainty.
news.means: The Trump-Xi meeting this month was the natural venue for a coordinated pause — both governments now treat the idea as a scare campaign instead. Don't bank on regulation slowing anything down soon.
news.source: The Rundown AI, The Neuron, Morning Brew, 1440 Daily Digest

news.body: Microsoft AI published a draft "Code of Conduct" for its own future models, built around CEO Mustafa Suleyman's "Humanist AI" stance: models must stop the moment a human pauses or shuts them down, stay inside the permissions actually granted, and never claim feelings, consciousness, or legal personhood.
news.means: A useful template for writing your own AI-usage guardrails into client engagements — but treat it as one vendor's aspiration, not an industry standard, until competing labs sign on.

news.body: Nvidia, Palantir, and Booz Allen Hamilton are reportedly limiting use of Anthropic's Fable on sensitive work, per The Information, because Anthropic keeps 30 days of usage logs; Microsoft is pitching worried clients on private servers instead.
news.means: If you're recommending an AI vendor to a client handling sensitive data, log retention just became a live differentiator — worth confirming before you make the call.

beyond_ai.body: EPA moves to repeal pollution limits on coal and gas power plants — a sector responsible for roughly a quarter of US climate pollution — saying the rollback saves industry over $300 billion; a separate proposed rule would argue greenhouse gases don't endanger public health, which could block future administrations from reinstating the rules.
beyond_ai.angle: Cheaper, dirtier power lines up with the tech industry's push for more energy for AI data centers — worth watching if any client's cost model assumes power prices keep falling.
beyond_ai.starter: If power gets cheaper because environmental rules just got rolled back, is anyone actually re-running their data-center cost assumptions?

beyond_ai.body: The 10-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5% Monday, the first time since 2023, as rising oil prices from the Iran conflict stoked inflation fears; it eased back below 5% before the close.
beyond_ai.angle: Higher yields mean higher borrowing costs — revisit any client business case built on cheap debt before your next budget conversation.
beyond_ai.starter: Is anyone still pricing client projects assuming last year's borrowing costs?

beyond_ai.body: Workers without a college degree are enjoying one of the best job markets in 20 years, while unemployment climbs for bachelor's-degree holders. The Burning Glass Institute ties it to fewer immigrant and retiring blue-collar workers, and AI is cited as replacing some entry-level white-collar roles.
beyond_ai.angle: A live data point for any workforce-planning conversation — entry-level hiring plans built around a degree requirement may need a second look.
beyond_ai.starter: Has anyone else noticed hiring managers getting more open to non-degree candidates lately, or is that just us?

beyond_ai.body: Houthi rebels captured two Red Sea islands and forced Saudi Arabia to shut a 750-mile oil pipeline for repairs, threatening a key oil-transit route through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; fighting has reportedly killed over 500 people and displaced roughly 94,000.
beyond_ai.angle: Another squeeze on oil supply on top of the existing Iran conflict — flag it for any client with global shipping or fuel-sensitive logistics costs.
beyond_ai.starter: With two separate Middle East chokepoints under pressure now, is anyone stress-testing shipping costs for next quarter?

beyond_ai.body: Apple TV's "Widow's Bay" swept the Emmys with 14 wins, a new record for a comedy series; Matthew Rhys became the first person to win lead-actor Emmys in two categories the same night, and Jean Smart won Best Actress in a Comedy for a fifth straight year on "Hacks."
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: Did you catch that Apple TV had the biggest night at the Emmys? Feels like the streaming wars keep shifting.
